paper_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
summary: A very deep image classifier made of stacked blocks of two 3×3 convolutions. Each block adds its own input back to its output through a shortcut, so it only has to learn a small correction, which makes networks with dozens or hundreds of layers trainable.

blocks.label: Input image
blocks.description: A randomly cropped, mean-subtracted RGB image enters the network.
blocks.source_quote: A 224 × 224 crop is randomly sampled from an image or its horizontal flip, with the per-pixel mean subtracted [21].

blocks.label: 7×7 conv, 64, /2 + BN + ReLU
blocks.description: A large strided stem convolution, followed by batch norm and ReLU, extracts low-level features and halves the resolution.
blocks.source_quote: We adopt batch normalization (BN) [16] right after each convolution and before activation, following [16].

blocks.label: 3×3 max pool, /2
blocks.description: Max pooling halves the spatial resolution again before the residual stages.
blocks.source_quote: 3 × 3 max pool, stride 2

blocks.label: 3×3 conv, 64 + BN + ReLU
blocks.description: The first layer of the residual function F: a convolution followed by batch norm and ReLU.
blocks.source_quote: The function F ( x , { W i } ) represents the residual mapping to be learned.

blocks.label: 3×3 conv, 64 + BN
blocks.description: The second convolution of F, followed by batch norm, completes the residual function.
blocks.source_quote: The baseline architectures are the same as the above plain nets, expect that a shortcut connection is added to each pair of 3 × 3 filters as in Fig. 3 (right).

blocks.label: Shortcut addition
blocks.description: Adds the block input, carried by an identity shortcut, to the residual output element-wise.
blocks.source_quote: The operation F + x is performed by a shortcut connection and element-wise addition.

blocks.label: ReLU
blocks.description: Applies a ReLU after the addition.
blocks.source_quote: We adopt the sec- ond nonlinearity after the addition ( i.e ., σ ( y ) , see Fig. 2).

blocks.label: 3×3 conv, 128 + BN + ReLU
blocks.description: The first residual convolution; in the first block of the stage it uses stride 2 to downsample and doubles the channels.
blocks.source_quote: We perform downsampling directly by convolutional layers that have a stride of 2.

blocks.label: 3×3 conv, 128 + BN
blocks.description: The second convolution of the residual function, followed by batch norm.
blocks.source_quote: The baseline architectures are the same as the above plain nets, expect that a shortcut connection is added to each pair of 3 × 3 filters as in Fig. 3 (right).

blocks.label: Shortcut addition
blocks.description: Adds the shortcut to the residual output; where dimensions increase, the shortcut is zero-padded (option A) or projected by a 1×1 convolution (option B).
blocks.source_quote: (B) The projection shortcut in Eqn.(2) is used to match dimensions (done by 1 × 1 convolutions).

blocks.label: ReLU
blocks.description: Applies a ReLU after the addition.
blocks.source_quote: We adopt the sec- ond nonlinearity after the addition ( i.e ., σ ( y ) , see Fig. 2).

blocks.label: 3×3 conv, 256 + BN + ReLU
blocks.description: The first residual convolution; the first block of the stage halves the resolution and doubles the filters.
blocks.source_quote: We perform downsampling directly by convolutional layers that have a stride of 2.

blocks.label: 3×3 conv, 256 + BN
blocks.description: The second convolution of the residual function, followed by batch norm.
blocks.source_quote: The baseline architectures are the same as the above plain nets, expect that a shortcut connection is added to each pair of 3 × 3 filters as in Fig. 3 (right).

blocks.label: Shortcut addition
blocks.description: Element-wise addition of the shortcut and the residual output.
blocks.source_quote: The operation F + x is performed by a shortcut connection and element-wise addition.

blocks.label: ReLU
blocks.description: Applies a ReLU after the addition.
blocks.source_quote: We adopt the sec- ond nonlinearity after the addition ( i.e ., σ ( y ) , see Fig. 2).

blocks.label: 3×3 conv, 512 + BN + ReLU
blocks.description: The first residual convolution; the first block of the stage halves the resolution and doubles the filters.
blocks.source_quote: We perform downsampling directly by convolutional layers that have a stride of 2.

blocks.label: 3×3 conv, 512 + BN
blocks.description: The second convolution of the residual function, followed by batch norm.
blocks.source_quote: The baseline architectures are the same as the above plain nets, expect that a shortcut connection is added to each pair of 3 × 3 filters as in Fig. 3 (right).

blocks.label: Shortcut addition
blocks.description: Element-wise addition of the shortcut and the residual output.
blocks.source_quote: The operation F + x is performed by a shortcut connection and element-wise addition.

blocks.label: ReLU
blocks.description: Applies a ReLU after the addition.
blocks.source_quote: We adopt the sec- ond nonlinearity after the addition ( i.e ., σ ( y ) , see Fig. 2).

blocks.label: Global average pool
blocks.description: Averages each feature map over all spatial positions into a single vector.
blocks.source_quote: The network ends with a global average pooling layer and a 1000-way fully-connected layer with softmax.

blocks.label: FC 1000
blocks.description: A fully-connected layer maps the pooled features to 1000 class scores.
blocks.source_quote: 1 × 1 average pool, 1000-d fc, softmax

blocks.label: Softmax
blocks.description: Converts the class scores into probabilities over the 1000 ImageNet classes.
blocks.source_quote: The network ends with a global average pooling layer and a 1000-way fully-connected layer with softmax.
